ICESat-2 detected a strong/fresh aerosols layer above cirrus clouds over southern Baffin Island at 06:43 UTC, September 4 and back trajectories point to the blowup location at the right time. THIS PYROCB WAS ADDED TO THE 2023 DATABASE ON APRIL 3, 2024 and to this database on April 5, 2025.

Very intense wildfire. Conditions for fire spread were extreme with relative humidity apparently as low as 8% and wind gusts of 61 mph. Second pyroCb pulse at 09:00 UTC. A sample of part of the smoke plume was detected thanks to the Asian Dust and Aerosol Lidar Observation Network (AD-Net; https://www-lidar.nies.go.jp/ctabc/). A suspicious layer was detected between 7-8 km (within the AI plume) over Jeju at ~06 UTC. Back trajectories point nicely to the area of the fire at about pyroCb time.

The plume moved east-northeast and dried out by 06 UTC. The many fires in the region produced an extensive, mostly low level smoke plume. The contribution of the pyroCb to the max AI is probably very small.

Two pulses. The plumes moved east-northeast and dried out by 04 UTC. The many fires in the region produced an extensive, mostly low level smoke plume.  The contribution of the pyroCb to the max AI is probably very small.

Two pulses. The second one started at 22:50 UTC. The coldest BT for the first pulse is -54.6 °C (NOAA 20 [JPSS-1] at 21:16 UTC). Both pulses produced a characteristic BTD signal and moved north-northwest during the first 12 hours.

This is an unusal case. The minimum BT of pyro-convection must be at least -40 °C to be entered in this database. In this case, the coldest BT is only -33 °C but lightning was generated. The Edwards AFB radar (KEYX) showed echoes at 34.5 kft (10.5 km) right over the fire at 20:18 and 20:22 UTC. The echoes had small rhoHV, so this is likely a pyroconvective turret. The start time in this case corresponds to 10 minutes before lightning was detected.

Small, short duration puff. The sun had already set when the convective cloud formed downstream of the fire. As a result, the SWIR was cold and of no help to confirm the presence of a pyroCb, nor was the slighly warm BTD. Thus the status of 'probable'.

Fire produced a a few stronger pulses. The first one was the most vigorous and resulted in a long lasting cold BT and warm BTD that moved across northern Manitoba, reached Hudson Bay around 12 UTC, August 28 and the border with Ontario around 16 UTC, August 28. The smoke pall from this pyroCb was still dense over southern James Bay at 13 UTC, August 29 and the southern Ontario - southern Québec border at 21:30 UTC, August 29. Coldest BT is colder than lowest temperature on sounding (-59.2 °C) so injection altitude is at least 12300 m.
